origin.description: Atkinson's inequality measure for a numeric vector.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Numeric vector. The measures are defined for non-negative values.

arguments.name: parameter
arguments.text: Inequality aversion. NULL uses 0.5. The value 1 uses the geometric mean.

arguments.name: na.rm
arguments.text: If true, drop missing values first. If false, any missing value makes the result missing.

origin.details: Parameter 1 is one minus the ratio of the geometric mean to the arithmetic mean. Any other parameter uses a power mean of the income shares. ineq() passes a NULL parameter through, so the default stays 0.5.
origin.example:
# generate vector (of incomes)
x <- c(541, 1463, 2445, 3438, 4437, 5401, 6392, 8304, 11904, 22261)
# compute Atkinson coefficient with parameter=0.5
ineq(x, parameter=0.5, type="Atkinson")

translation.description: Atkinson's inequality measure for a numeric vector.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Numeric vector. The measures are defined for non-negative values. Missing values are NaN.

arguments.name: parameter
arguments.text: Inequality aversion. None uses 0.5. The value 1 uses the geometric mean.

arguments.name: na_rm
arguments.text: If true, drop missing values first. If false, any missing value makes the result NaN.

translation.details: Parameter 1 is one minus the ratio of the geometric mean to the arithmetic mean. Any other parameter uses a power mean of the income shares. ineq() passes parameter None through, so the default stays 0.5.
translation.example:
from ineq.measures import ineq

# generate vector (of incomes)
x = [541, 1463, 2445, 3438, 4437, 5401, 6392, 8304, 11904, 22261]
# compute Atkinson coefficient with parameter=0.5
print(ineq(x, parameter=0.5, type="Atkinson"))
